context: Mirror whatever fix test-export-invalid-output-dir-assumes-non-root settles on, so all three read consistently: either construct a path whose creation fails regardless of privilege, or guard on euid with a recorded reason. Do not weaken what each test proves - the exporter, the dry run, and the probe must still be shown to surface an error rather than reporting success.
description: test-export-invalid-output-dir-assumes-non-root records that test_export_with_invalid_output_dir cannot pass as root, but its only_modify is tests/unit/cli/test_cli_output.py, so it fixes one of three tests with the same root cause. The other two fail identically in a root container and are not covered by any item. test_cli_dryrun.py TestDryRunErrorHandling test_dry_run_with_missing_output_dir expects an uncreatable output directory, which root can create. test_file_format.py TestHasTrailingDelimiterSurfacesReadFailures test_unreadable_file_raises_rather_than_reporting_clean chmods a file to 0o000 and expects OSError, which root bypasses entirely. Both were confirmed failing on clean origin/develop at a1e1328 with no local changes, so neither is caused by recent work; the file_format one in particular is NOT a defect in trailing-delimiter-probe-swallows-read-errors, whose product behavior is correct. Real CI is unaffected because its runners are not root, so this only bites container and remote agent sessions - where it costs every session the work of re-deriving that the failures are environmental.

preserves.behavior: Each test still proves its subject raises rather than silently reporting success

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/cli/test_cli_dryrun.py tests/unit/utils/test_file_format.py -q
verifications.description: Both files pass in a root container without weakening their assertions

work_units.summary: Confirm both tests fail as root and pass as non-root on current develop
